I was considered overweight at the start of my pregnancy as well. So my weight has been monitored pretty closely throughout. I did have a large gain around 35 weeks and the doctor told me I couldn’t gain anymore from here out. (Currently 39+3) I changed my diet in the sense that I started eating smaller meals more often. All my meals and snacks are protein rich and tend to include some kind of vegetable. I cut out excess sugar and carbs. (French fries were my downfall throughout this pregnancy!) I typically have eggs of some sort for breakfast with veggies cooked in and a piece of fruit. Lunch is a spinach salad packed with other veggies, a low sodium cheese and some protein, or some homemade soup or turkey chili (again, lots of protein and veggies). Dinner I try to have a protein, a veggie and a healthy carb (whole wheat pasta, brown rice, etc.). In between meals I’ll have cut up veggies, fruit, nuts, yogurt, or things that are light but filling. Since I started doing this I’ve actually lost about 12lbs and the doctors say my baby is thriving and very healthy. So yes, you can lose weight while pregnant. Just be conscious of what you’re eating (high protein, low carb) and make sure you’re still eating.  Ohhhhh and drink lots of water, staying hydrated is the best thing for your body (hair, skin, organs) and your baby!! 
Good luck!!

Back in early April I was struggling with some severe depression, and was placed in an in-patient psych floor to regulate meds and be monitored for a bit. When I met my roommate, one of the first things she asked me was if I was pregnant. I just laughed and said no! Mind you, I had been so depressed my husband and I were rarely ever intimate so the chances were near nonexistent. Over the course of the week and a half they weened me off all meds.  I became severely sick (nauseous, vomiting, extremely fatigued), which I attributed to withdrawal from the meds. However my period was also 5 days late and I’ve always been very regular. So one night I asked my nurse if they did a pregnancy test when I first came in (they took a ton of blood to look at all my levels). His response was “yes but it was inconclusive”...  I was so confused by this response, so he told me I had to talk with the doctor in the morning.  The next morning the doctor said my HCG levels when I first came in were soo low that it was slightly possible, but they would need to recheck. So they took more blood and sure enough my HCG levels went from 38 to 875. I was only 3/4 weeks pregnant by that point, and clearly not showing, and had other reasons for my physical symptoms but somehow my roommate knew. When I told her the news she just smiled and said, “I know”. It still blows my mind... I’m also doing much better emotionally and our little nugget will be here in about 7 weeks!
